title: Concurrent agents fan out onto one shared provider quota with no admission control
problem: My batch of agents worked when I ran two of them and produced nothing at all when I ran eight, because every one of them was drawing on the same provider account and none of them knew the others existed.
symptom: Every task in the batch fails with the same connection-stall or service-busy error, no single agent logs anything wrong, and the only way to see it is to count the live agent processes against one account.
why_now: Agent frameworks expose per-call retry settings and per-pool worker counts, but no shared admission control across independently launched agents. Fan-out is one line of code and the quota it consumes is process-global, so the limit that binds is invisible at the call site.
existing: Per-pool worker counts (ThreadPoolExecutor max_workers): bound one pool, not the sum of independently launched pools.
Provider-side rate limit headers: report the ceiling after you have hit it, and give a losing agent no way to yield.
Manual pre-flight process counting: works, but it is a human ritual with no runtime enforcement.

evidence.title: INC-0011: Concurrent agent brains silently starve and kill each other
evidence.quote: One provider account, N concurrent brains fighting for it. Each brain retries on failure, which manufactures more concurrent load, which starves the others further.
evidence.note: First-hand incident: an 8-task batch failed 8/8 across 5 retries each with zero output, launched into an account already running an always-on dispatcher.

build_hypothesis: A host-level admission token shared by every agent process against one provider account: a small daemon or lock-file lease that a launcher must acquire before adding concurrency, so an extra agent waits instead of starving the ones already running.

check.manual_question: This code fans out concurrent model calls. If a second copy of it, or another agent loop, is already running against the same provider account, what bounds the TOTAL in-flight requests rather than the fan-out of this one process?
check.rationale: Concurrent fan-out plus no lexical trace of any concurrency bound is the signature of unbounded admission against a shared quota. It can be wrong when the bound lives outside the repo (a gateway or a proxy), which is why the absence of a bound is a finding to look at rather than a fault, and the presence of one is credited as a mitigation.

bad.fanout.py:
import asyncio
from anthropic import Anthropic

client = Anthropic()


async def one(task):
    return client.messages.create(model="m", messages=task)


async def run_all(tasks):
    return await asyncio.gather(*[one(t) for t in tasks])

good.fanout.py:
import asyncio
from anthropic import Anthropic

client = Anthropic()

# Admission control shared by every caller in this process against one account.
GATE = asyncio.Semaphore(2)


async def one(task):
    async with GATE:
        return client.messages.create(model="m", messages=task)


async def run_all(tasks):
    return await asyncio.gather(*[one(t) for t in tasks])
